text:
Saturday
Football
8am (all times GMT)Matchday live
The international break is over as domestic football boogies back. Primed to feel the force is Dominic Booth at the helm of our essential gateway to the weekend’s action. Saturday offers a magnificent seven Premier League matches, bookended by Manchester City v Fulham and Newcastle v Arsenal. There is also a full programme of Championship, League One, and League Two fixtures, plus Celtic and Rangers taking to the Glasgow greensward in Scotland. In the WSL, Liverpool host Chelsea before rich kids London City prepare to receive Crystal Palace. For breaking news, reader input and good vibes aplenty – join the conversation at matchday.live@theguardian.com.
T20 cricket
8.15am Australia v England live
To the background buzz of Australian cricket ripping itself apart over sandpapergate, England kick off their T20 series at the same venue they became world champions four years ago. The Melbourne Cricket Ground has not always been a happy hunting ground for touring England sides but Harry Brook’s last two visits as captain have been triumphant. A two-day win at the 90,000-capacity venue in last year’s Boxing Day Test was not only the high point of a traumatic Ashes campaign; it was their first red-ball victory on Australian soil since 2011. MCG also hosted England’s T20 World Cup triumph in 2022, where Brook was part of the side that defeated Pakistan to lift the trophy behind enemy lines. Rob Smyth has over-by-over coverage with Ali Martin reporting from Melbourne.
Premier League
12.30pmManchester City v Fulham live
The lunchtime kick-off is a vital one for the hosts. City have wobbled of late, three straight Premier League defeats leave the beleaguered club in third with 21 points from the first 10 games of Enzo Maresca’s tenure. In stark contrast, the Cottagers are unbeaten in their last four games, after four defeats and two draws in their first six. Wins over Hull and Coventry came before draws with Aston Villa and Newcastle. Barry Glendenning helms the blog as Will Unwin reports from the Etihad Stadium.
Rugby union
2.10pmEngland v New Zealand
England are have been transformed since stumbling through the Six Nations and then falling to South Africa at Ellis Park, winning four consecutive Tests, amassing 36 tries and addressing their disciplinary lapses. Aided by thumping victories over Fiji and Japan, they have rebuilt impressively to secure a shot at reaching the Nations Championship final, but New Zealand provide the true measure of their progress. Only South Africa are higher in the rankings and a year out from the 2027 World Cup final, it is the opportunity for Steve Borthwick’s men to make a statement. Lee Calvert blogs the action and the trio of Robert Kitson, Andy Bull and Gerard Meagher making up our Twickenham reporting team.
Tennis
2.30pmATP Finals live
Katy Murrells is at the controls of our tennis liveblog as the semi-finals pan out in Turin. The first session starts at 2.30pm, with the evening match due to start at about 8.30pm.
Premier League
3pmClockwatch
Emillia Hawkins keeps the updates flowing on the five afternoon kick-offs: Aston Villa v Sunderland, Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Chelsea v Leeds, Coventry v Crystal Palace, and Tottenham v Ipswich – the pick of the bunch. Roberto De Zerbi seemed to be making an impact at Spurs before a defeat by Leeds tripped up his side. Their record is grim against the Tractor Boys: four defeats in their last five Premier league games.
Rugby union
4.40pmIreland v South Africa live
Lee Calvert is back on deck as Ireland risk a Springbok backlash from a side bruised by defeat by France and furious at their coach, Rassie Erasmus, for getting banned after his incendiary “match-fixing” comments. There is more at stake in this November’s meeting between the sides than last year’s chaotic Test. The Irish were down to 12 men at one stage and the Springboks won 24-13 for their first win in Dublin since 2012. Both countries are still in the running to top their respective pools and play in the final on Finals weekend at Twickenham. Brendan Fanning reports. 
Premier League
 5.30pmNewcastle v Arsenal live
City’s slump has allowed the defending champions, Arsenal, to seize early control and they will hope to continue their relentless start to the season. They head to Newcastle where a toxic reception awaits Bruno Guimarães as he returns to Tyneside in Arsenal colours for the first time since his summer move. The Gunners are five points clear of second-placed Brighton at the top after winning nine of their first 10 games. Matthias Jaissle’s inconsistent hosts have managed just one win in their past five league matches, losing to Everton and Aston Villa along the way. Join Rob Smyth for MBM commentary, with Louis Taylor reporting.
Sunday
Formula One
4amLas Vegas Grand Prix
Kimi Antonelli may have already won the drivers’ crown, but second place in the standings is still up for grabs and Max Verstappen can tighten his grip in Sin City. The Red Bull driver is 17 points clear of Mercedes’ George Russell, who moved back up to third place, one point ahead of Lewis Hamilton after his fourth place at Interlagos. Krishani Dhanji be live blogging the race in the small hours, with Giles Richards reporting from Las Vegas.
Football
8amMatchday live
Dominic Booth and Emillia Hawkins clock on with all the latest news and reader views for a Sunday featuring the Premier League fixture of the weekend. Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United at Anfield just days after wrapping up his reign as USA men’s coach. Victory would give him instant momentum as he fights to lift the club up the table. Earlier, hard-charging Brighton will fancy their chances against Hull, who have not won a Premier League match since August. For breaking news, reader input and good vibes aplenty – join the conversation at matchday.live@theguardian.com.
Women’s Super League
12pmWSL clockwatch 
Emillia Hawkins and John Brewin keep track of Sunday’s WSL fixtures from midday as Birmingham face Manchester United and Charlton host Aston Villa. Then it is Everton v Brighton at 2pm followed by a London derby as Rita Guarino’s in-form West Ham visit Arsenal, with the Irons having notched four wins in their past five matches in all competitions. The Gunners are toiling, and they sit sixth in the standings going into the weekend, with just three wins from their opening 10 matches. 
Premier League
2pmHull v Brighton live
Second-placed Brighton have become the most unlikely title contenders with their free-scoring football and have every chance of continuing to defy the sceptics as they take on Hull. The Seagulls are the league’s top scorers with 26 goals, 11 more than Arsenal, and have the second-tightest defence, with just seven goals conceded.Join Dominic Booth for minute-by-minute coverage, with Aaron Bower reporting from MKM Stadium.
Premier League
4.30pmLiverpool v Manchester United
Rob Smyth buckles up for the big one at Anfield with all eyes on the latest United manager, Mauricio Pochettino. United’s tally of eight points and one win after 10 games is their lowest at this stage of a league season for 40 years. The former Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea manager says he needs time to turn the dysfunctional club’s fortunes around but he will be aware of the need to show progress quickly, with Liverpool in no mood to offer their most bitter rivals any favours. Looking for omens? The Argentinian’s first game for Chelsea was against Liverpool, which ended in a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge. Andy Hunter and Jamie Jackson make up our reporting team on Merseyside.
Tennis
TBCATP Finals final 
Daniel Harris offers live coverage of the final from Turin as the season-ending indoor hard-court tournament featuring the top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams draws to a thrilling close.
American football
6pmNFL Week 11 live
Graham Searles returns with his essential NFL liveblog covering the seven 6pm clashes. The division-leading Buffalo Bills (8-1), who boast the top scoring offence and second-best rush attack in the NFL, meet the Miami Dolphins (1-8) in the big AFC East clash. The other early Sunday games are Bears v Saints, Lions v Buccaneers, Panthers v Ravens, Cowboys v Titans, Chiefs v Cardinals, and Eagles v Steelers.
